meta_title: Integrate x log(1+2x) 0 to 1 — NCERT Exemplar Q45
meta_desc: Step-by-step integration by parts for NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Q45: evaluate x log(1+2x) from 0 to 1, get 3/8 log 3, plus a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Integration by Parts (Log Factor) Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions built around NCERT Exemplar Q45 — choosing u and dv, running the by-parts step, and finishing the leftover rational integral. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Definite integration by parts with a logarithmic factor

questions.q: For ∫₀¹ x·log(1+2x) dx, which choice for integration by parts is correct?
questions.explanation: By ILATE the logarithmic function is differentiated, so u = log(1+2x) and dv = x dx. Differentiating the log removes it from the next integral.

questions.q: If u = log(1+2x), then du equals?
questions.explanation: d/dx log(1+2x) = (1/(1+2x))·2 by the chain rule, so du = 2/(1+2x) dx.

questions.q: With dv = x dx, what is v?
questions.explanation: v = ∫ x dx = x²/2 (the constant is dropped in by-parts).

questions.q: The integration by parts formula ∫ u dv equals?
questions.explanation: The standard formula is ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du.

questions.q: After one by-parts step the leftover is (1/2)log 3 − ∫₀¹ ( ? ) dx. What is the integrand?
questions.explanation: v du = (x²/2)·(2/(1+2x)) dx = x²/(1+2x) dx, so that fraction is subtracted.
At x=1: (1/2)log 3; at x=0: (0)·log 1 = 0. So the term is (1/2) log 3.

questions.q: To integrate x²/(1+2x), what is the correct first step?
options: Reduce the improper fraction by dividing
Split into two linear partial fractions
questions.explanation: The numerator degree is not less than the denominator, so divide first: x²/(1+2x) = x/2 − 1/4 + (1/4)/(1+2x).

questions.q: The value of ∫₀¹ x·log(1+2x) dx is?
questions.explanation: The result is (1/2)log 3 − (1/8)log 3 = (3/8) log 3, since the rational integral equals (1/8) log 3.

faq.q: Why is log(1+2x) chosen as u and not x?
faq.a: The ILATE order puts the logarithmic function ahead of the algebraic one, so log(1+2x) becomes u and gets differentiated. Its derivative, 2/(1+2x), is far easier to handle than trying to integrate a logarithm.

faq.q: How do you integrate x²/(1+2x) that appears in the second step?
faq.a: It is an improper fraction, so divide first: x²/(1+2x) = x/2 − 1/4 + (1/4)/(1+2x). Integrating term by term from 0 to 1 gives (1/8) log 3.

faq.q: What is the final answer to this NCERT Exemplar Q45 integral?
faq.a: The definite integral of x·log(1+2x) from 0 to 1 equals (3/8) log 3, which is roughly 0.412.

faq.q: Do the limits change when using integration by parts?
faq.a: No. In a definite integral by parts the limits stay 0 to 1 throughout; you evaluate the boundary term uv at both limits and keep the same limits on the remaining integral.
